بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ

سُورَةُ قُرَيْشٍ

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لِإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾ ﴿إيلافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ والصَّيْفِ﴾.

In the Lord's words, "For the covenant (ī'lāf) of Quraysh, their covenant of the caravan journeys of winter and summer" [Quraysh 106:1–2].

اخْتُلِفَ في اللّامِ في ﴿لِإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾، هَلْ هي مُتَعَلِّقَةٌ بِما قَبْلَها، وعَلى أيِّ مَعْنًى. أمْ مُتَعَلِّقَةٌ بِما بَعْدَها، وعَلى أيِّ مَعْنًى.

Scholars differed concerning the lām in "li-īlāfi Quraysh": whether it is connected to what precedes it, and in what sense; or whether it is connected to what follows it, and in what sense.

فَمَن قالَ: مُتَعَلِّقَةٌ بِما قَبْلَها، قالَ مُتَعَلِّقَةٌ بِجَعَلَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَجَعَلَهم كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ﴾ [الفيل: ٥].

Whoever said it is connected to what precedes it said it is connected to "ja'alahum" (He made them) in the Lord's words, "and He made them like eaten stalks" [al-Fil 105:5].

وَتَكُونُ بِمَعْنى لِأجْلِ إيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ يَدُومُ لَهم ويَبْقى تَعْظِيمُ العَرَبِ إيّاهم؛ لِأنَّهم أهْلُ حَرَمِ اللَّهِ، أوْ بِمَعْنى إلى أيْ جَعَلْنا العَدُوَّ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ، هَزِيمَةً لَهُ ونُصْرَةً لِقُرَيْشٍ نِعْمَةً عَلَيْهِمْ، إلى نِعْمَةِ إيلافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ والصَّيْفِ.

The lām then means "for the sake of," so that the Arabs' reverence for them would continue and endure, because they are the people of God's Sacred House; or it means "toward," i.e., We made the enemy like eaten stalks as a defeat for him and a victory for Quraysh, a blessing upon them, leading to the blessing of their covenant of the caravan journeys of winter and summer.

وَمَن قالَ: مُتَعَلِّقَةٌ بِما بَعْدَها، قالَ ﴿لِإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾ ﴿إيلافِهِمْ﴾ الَّذِي ألِفُوهُ أيْ بِمَثابَةِ التَّقْرِيرِ لَهُ، ورَتَّبَ عَلَيْهِ، ﴿فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَذا البَيْتِ﴾. أيْ أثْبَتَهُ إلَيْهِمْ وحَفِظَهُ لَهم.

Whoever said it is connected to what follows it said that "li-īlāfi Quraysh, īlāfihim" (for the covenant of Quraysh, their covenant that they had established) serves as an affirmation of it, and that the following is built upon it: "so let them worship the Lord of this House" [Quraysh 106:3]. That is, He attributed it to them and preserved it for them.

وَهَذا القَوْلُ الأخِيرُ هو اخْتِيارُ ابْنِ جَرِيرٍ، ورَواهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، ورَدَ جَوازَ القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ؛ لِأنَّهُ يَلْزَمُهُ فَصْلُ السُّورَتَيْنِ عَنْ بَعْضٍ.

This last view is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and it was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. He rejected the permissibility of the first view, because it entails separating the two surahs from one another.

وَقِيلَ: إنَّها لِلتَّعَجُّبِ، أيِ اعْجَبُوا لِإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ، حَكاهُ القُرْطُبِيُّ عَنِ الكِسائِيِّ والأخْفَشِ، والقَوْلُ الأوَّلُ لِغَيْرِهِ.

It was also said that the lām is for wonder, meaning, "Wonder at the covenant of Quraysh." Al-Qurtubi related this from al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash, and the first view belongs to others.

وَرُوِيَ أيْضًا عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وغَيْرِهِ، واسْتَدَلُّوا بِقِراءَةِ السُّورَتَيْنِ مَعًا في الصَّلاةِ في رَكْعَةٍ قَرَأ بِهِما عُمَرُ بْنُ الخَطّابِ، وبِأنَّ السُّورَتَيْنِ في أُبَيِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ مُتَّصِلَتانِ، ولا فَصْلَ بَيْنَهُما.

This was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and others, and they cited that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recited both surahs together in one rak'ah of prayer, and that in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b the two surahs are joined with no separation between them.

وَحَكى القُرْطُبِيُّ القَوْلَيْنِ، ولَمْ يُرَجِّحْ أحَدَهُما، ولا يَبْعُدِ اعْتِبارُ الوَجْهَيْنِ، لِأنَّهُ لا يُعارِضُ بَعْضُها بَعْضًا.

Al-Qurtubi related the two views without preferring either, and it is not far-fetched to consider both meanings, since they do not contradict one another.

(p-١١٠)وَما اعْتَرَضَ بِهِ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ بِأنَّهُ يُلْزِمُ عَلَيْهِ اتِّصالَ السُّورَتَيْنِ فَلَيْسَ بِلازِمٍ؛ لِأنَّهُ إنْ أرادَ اتِّصالَهُما في المَعْنى، فالقُرْآنُ كُلُّهُ مُتَّصِلَةٌ سُوَرُهُ مَعْنًى.

As for Ibn Jarir's objection, that it entails the joining of the two surahs, it does not necessarily follow; for if he means their joining in meaning, then the whole Qur'an has surahs connected in meaning.

ألّا تَرى إلى فاتِحَةِ الكِتابِ وفِيها ﴿اهْدِنا الصِّراطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ﴾ [الفاتحة: ٦]، فَجاءَتْ سُورَةُ البَقَرَةِ: ﴿ذَلِكَ الكِتابُ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾ [البقرة: ٢]، وبَعْدَها ذَكَرَ أوْصافَهم وقالَ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَلى هُدًى مِن رَبِّهِمْ﴾ [البقرة: ٥]، فَأيُّ ارْتِباطٍ أقْوى مِن هَذا، كَأنَّهُ يَقُولُ: الهُدى الَّذِي تَطْلُبُونَهُ في هَذا الكِتابِ فَهو هُدًى لِلْمُتَّقِينَ، وإنْ أرادَ اتِّصالًا حَسًا بِعَدَمِ البَسْمَلَةِ، فَنَظِيرُها سُورَةُ بَراءَةٌ مَعَ الأنْفالِ، ولَكِنْ لا حاجَةَ إلى ذَلِكَ؛ لِأنَّ إجْماعَ القُرّاءِ عَلى إثْباتِ البَسْمَلَةِ بَيْنَهُما، اللَّهُمَّ إلّا مُصْحَفَ أُبَيِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ، ولَيْسَ في هَذَيْنِ الوَجْهَيْنِ وجْهٌ أرْجَحَ مِن وجْهٍ.

Do you not see the Opening of the Book, in which is "Guide us to the straight path" [al-Fatihah 1:6], and then comes the surah of al-Baqarah: "This is the Book, there is no doubt in it" [al-Baqarah 2:2], and after it He mentions their attributes and says: "Those are upon guidance from their Lord" [al-Baqarah 2:5]? What connection is stronger than this? It is as if He says: the guidance you seek in this Book is guidance for the God-fearing. As for a connection in form by the absence of the basmalah, its parallel is the surah of Bara'ah with al-Anfal; but there is no need for that, since the reciters agree on affirming the basmalah between them, except in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Neither of these two views has a preference over the other.

وَلِذا لَمْ يُرَجِّحْ بَيْنَهُما أحَدٌ مِنَ المُفَسِّرِينَ، سِوى ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ:

For this reason none of the exegetes preferred between them, except Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him:

وَصِحَّةُ الوَجْهَيْنِ أقْوى وأعَمُّ في الِامْتِنانِ وتَعْدادِ النِّعَمِ.

"The soundness of both views is stronger and more comprehensive in conferring favor and enumerating blessings."

والإيلافُ: قِيلَ مِنَ التَّأْلِيفِ، إذْ كانُوا في رِحْلَتَيْهِمْ يَأْلَفُونَ المُلُوكَ في الشّامِ واليَمَنِ، أوْ كانُوا هم في أنْفُسِهِمْ مُؤَلَّفِينَ ومُجَمَّعِينَ، وهو امْتِنانٌ عَلَيْهِمْ بِهَذا التَّجَمُّعِ والتَّألُّفِ، ولَوْ سَلَّطَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَفَرَّقَهم وشَتَّتَهم، وأنْشَدُوا:

As for "īlāf" (covenant), it was said to derive from ta'lif (bringing together), since in their two journeys they would bring together the kings in al-Sham and Yemen; or that they themselves were brought together and gathered; and this is a favor upon them through this gathering and unity, for had He given power over them, He would have scattered and dispersed them. And they recited:

؎أبُونا قُصَيٌّ كانَ يُدْعى مُجَمِّعًا بِهِ جَمَعَ اللَّهُ القَبائِلَ مِن فِهْر

"Our father Qusayy was called 'the Gatherer,' by him God gathered the tribes from Fihr."

وَقِيلَ: مِنَ الإلْفِ والتَّعَوُّدِ، أيْ: ألِفُوا الرِّحْلَتَيْنِ.

It was also said that it derives from ulf (familiarity and habit), that is, they were accustomed to the two journeys.

فَلِلْإبْقاءِ لَهم عَلى ما ألِفُوهُ.

So it refers to preserving for them what they were accustomed to.

وَقُرَيْشٌ قالَ أبُو حَيّانَ: عَلَمٌ عَلى القَبِيلَةِ.

As for "Quraysh," Abu Hayyan said it is a proper name for the tribe.

وَقِيلَ: أصْلُها مِنَ النَّقْرَشِ، وهو الِاجْتِماعُ أوِ التَّكَسُّبُ والجَمْعُ.

It was said that its root is from naqrash, which means gathering, or earning and collecting.

وَقِيلَ: مِن دابَّةِ البَحْرِ المُسَمّاةِ بِالقِرْشِ وهي أخْطَرُ حَيَواناتِهِ، وهو مَرْوِيٌّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ في جَوابِهِ لِمُعاوِيَةَ.

It was said that it is from the sea creature called the qirsh, which is the most dangerous of sea animals; this is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas in his answer to Mu'awiyah.

وَأنْشَدَ قَوْلَ الشّاعِرِ:

He recited the words of the poet:

؎وَقُرَيْشٌ هي الَّتِي تَسْكُنُ البَحْـ ∗∗∗ ـرَ بِها سُمِّيَتْ قُرَيْشٌ قُرَيْشا

"Quraysh is the one that dwells in the sea; by it Quraysh was named Quraysh."

؎(p-١١١)تَأْكُلُ الرَّثَّ والسَّمِينَ ولا ∗∗∗ تَتْرُكُ فِيها لِذِي جَناحَيْنِ رِيشًا

"It devours the worn and the fat, and leaves in it for the two-winged one no feather."

؎هَكَذا في البِلادِ حَيُّ قُرَيْشٍ ∗∗∗ يَأْكُلُونَ البِلادَ أكْلًا كَمِيشا

"Thus in the lands is the tribe of Quraysh, devouring the lands with a severe devouring."

؎وَلَهم آخِرُ الزَّمانِ نَبِيٌّ ∗∗∗ يُكْثِرُ القَتْلَ فِيهِمْ والخُمُوشا

"And for them at the end of time is a prophet who multiplies slaying and scratching among them."

وَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ والصَّيْفِ﴾، هو تَفْسِيرٌ ”لِإيلافِ“ سَواءٌ عَلى ما كانُوا يُؤالِفُونَ بَيْنَ المُلُوكِ في تِلْكَ الرَّحَلاتِ، أوْ ما كانُوا يَأْلَفُونَهُ فِيهِما.

The Lord's words, "the caravan journeys of winter and summer," are an explanation of "īlāf," whether it refers to what they brought together among the kings in those journeys, or to what they were accustomed to in them.

Allah's saying: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House.﴾

What is meant by "the House" is the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram, the Ka'bah), as it appears in the supplication of Ibrahim, upon him and upon our Prophet be blessings and peace: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House.﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 106, verse 4:

Allah's saying: ﴿Who has fed them against hunger and made them secure against fear.﴾

This serves as the reason (ta'lil) for the requirement of worshipping Him, because He, glory be to Him, is the One who arranged for them these two journeys, which were the means of those blessings upon them. So it was their duty to thank Him for His blessings and to worship Him alone.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, had already explained this meaning at the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 67], and he cited the texts with this meaning in a way that made repeating it unnecessary.

Note

In His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House﴾ ﴿Who has fed them against hunger and made them secure against fear﴾, He linked the blessing with its requirement, as a link between cause and effect.

Therein is a clarification of the requirement of worshipping Allah alone, and of His right over His servants all together, and it is not specific to the Quraysh.

This right was established by the first word in the Qur'an and the first call in the Mushaf. The first is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatiha: 2], as if He were saying: He, glory be to Him, deserves praise, because He is the Lord of the worlds, that is, their Creator, their Provider, their Merciful One, and so on.

(p-112) The second is: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord﴾ [al-Baqara: 21].

Then He clarified the requirement by His saying: ﴿Who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous﴾ [al-Baqara: 21].

Then He enumerated His blessings upon them by His saying: ﴿Who made for you the earth a bed and the sky a canopy, and sent down from the sky water and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾ [al-Baqara: 22].

So these blessings are equivalent to feeding them against hunger and securing them against fear, with regard to the Quraysh. Among this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾ ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ [al-Kawthar: 1-2].

Allah, the Exalted, has also made clear that gratitude increases blessings and disbelief takes them away, except what is a gradual trap (istidraj). He said regarding the thanks for a blessing: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

And He said regarding ingratitude and its consequences: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a city which was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it in abundance from every place, but it denied the favours of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 112].

On this occasion, it is incumbent upon every Muslim, individuals and communities, to meet the blessings of Allah with gratitude, to thank them by obedience and worship of Allah, and to beware of ungratefulness for blessings.

Another note

In the combination of their being fed against hunger and secured against fear, there is a great blessing, because a person does not enjoy ease or happiness except by attaining these two blessings together, for there is no living with hunger and no security with fear, and the blessing is completed by their combination.

For this reason the hadith came: "Whoever wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his home, having his food for the day, it is as though the whole world has been gathered for him."

Another note

In this surah there is evidence that the supplication of the prophets is answered, because the Friend (Khalil), upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace, supplicated for the people of the Sanctuary, saying: ﴿So make hearts from among the people incline toward them, and provide for them from the fruits﴾ [Ibrahim: 37].

(p-113) And he said: ﴿Our Lord, raise up among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses﴾ [al-Baqara: 129]. So Allah fed them against hunger and secured them against fear, and sent among them a messenger from themselves who recites to them His verses.
